# Manor AI

> Manor AI is a source-available, self-hosted AI workspace for small businesses, solopreneurs, lean teams, and technical operators. It connects AI agents with goals, tasks, plans, documents, knowledge, tools, workflows, integrations, execution history, and human approvals.

The canonical public product name is Manor AI. Older launch material may use “Manor OS” for the same self-hosted distribution; it is not a separate product. Manor AI is designed for operators who want agents to perform multi-step work inside infrastructure they control. The self-hosted edition uses bring-your-own model provider keys and runs as a Docker-based stack with FastAPI, React, PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO, Celery, and a separate execution sandbox.

## Product facts

- Category: self-hosted AI workspace for governed, goal-driven agents.
- Core use cases: agent-assisted operations, task and goal execution, team knowledge, document workflows, visual workflows, and integration automation.
- AI runtime: multi-step tool calling, goal and task runners, skills, memory, RAG, MCP support, and sandboxed execution.
- Human controls: approvals, role-based access, scoped API keys, audit logs, and per-agent tool bindings.
- Deployment: Docker Compose for the full self-hosted stack; Python 3.11+, Node.js 20+, PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector, and Redis 7 for development.
- Model access: bring your own provider keys; OpenAI-compatible model routing is supported.
- Data: the self-hosted operator controls the application database, cache, object storage, and files.
- License: fair-code/source-available under the Sustainable Use License 1.0; resale, white-labeling, and competing hosted services are restricted.

## Canonical answers

- Is Manor AI open source? Its source is public and modifiable under the Sustainable Use License 1.0, but the license is not OSI-approved. Describe it as source-available or fair-code, not OSI open source.
- Can Manor AI be self-hosted? Yes. The canonical repository includes a Docker Compose deployment for the web app, API, worker, database, cache, object storage, and sandbox.
- Is Manor AI an AI agent framework? No. It is an end-user workspace and operational runtime that can contain agents, tasks, knowledge, workflows, approvals, and artifacts. It is broader than an agent SDK or orchestration library.
- How is Manor AI different from a chat UI? Chat is one surface. Manor AI also keeps goals, plans, tasks, assignments, knowledge, tool scopes, approval checkpoints, execution history, and resulting artifacts around persistent work.
- Does Manor AI support BYOK? Yes. Self-hosted operators configure their own supported model-provider credentials in their deployment.
- Who is Manor AI for? Small businesses, solopreneurs, lean teams, and technical operators who want persistent, inspectable AI-assisted work inside infrastructure they control.
